intentions.title: Turn the codebase itself into a navigable Barkpark graph — one paper per file, with real dependency/intention/co-change edges, so the codebase can be browsed and queried like content
intentions.evidence: tooling/barkpark-sync/generate.mjs builds nodes.json (one node per code file, quality metrics + content + deps); push.mjs creates/publishes a `paper` per file with typed reference fields (dependencies, intentions) into an isolated `codebase` dataset; graph-view.mjs renders it; push.mjs explicitly refuses `--dataset production` to prevent code papers leaking into prod content.

intentions.title: Score codebase quality on programmatic, non-fabricated signals — reach, churn, defects, real test coverage, ownership, consistency — and roll them into one auditable grade with ranked worklists
intentions.evidence: tooling/quality/quality.mjs computes four composites (HOTSPOT, PRIORITY, REFACTOR-WORTH, CRITICAL-UNTESTED) from risk-report.json, ergonomics-report.json, consistency-report.json, aesthetics-report.json; explicit comments reject 'false 100' fabrication when reports are missing (covReport, cite default to null/clean rather than 0/100 fakery); tooling/risk/risk.mjs measures REAL go/mix coverage (not proxy) and defect density via git bug-fix-word mining.

intentions.title: Calibrate the scoring formulas themselves from the codebase's own git history instead of hand-tuned weights, so composite scores are learned and validated (AUC, temporal cross-validation) rather than asserted
intentions.evidence: tooling/fit/fit.mjs: assembles a per-file signal matrix, derives a 'future-defect' outcome label from git history, fits logistic-regression weights, flags collinearity (|r|>0.7), and cross-validates on a held-out recent window; outputs scoring-config.json consumed by quality.mjs's composites.

intentions.title: Cross-validate every relationship the graph asserts (file-to-file deps, file-to-task scope, co-change pairs) against ACTUAL git/commit evidence, so predicted structure never silently drifts from reality
intentions.evidence: tooling/cochange/cochange.mjs (relationship cross-validation, 'accidental coupling'); tooling/tasks/tasks.mjs computes predicted∩actual/predicted−actual/actual−predicted per task by diffing commit-message-grepped files against intention-inherited scope; consistency.mjs flags deviation-from-group-norm as the definition of inconsistency.

intentions.title: Provide a single idempotent orchestration entrypoint (status.mjs) that runs the full ASSESS→ENRICH→PUBLISH pipeline for free (zero tokens) and only asks an agent for judgment work a parser genuinely can't do
intentions.evidence: tooling/status/status.mjs runs blast-index, signals, ergonomics, risk, deps, consistency, aesthetics, coverage, combined, quality, then usefulness/intentions merges and generate/push, gated on a content hash (`nodesHash !== lastHash`) so unchanged work costs nothing; reports 'pending agent work' per arc rather than doing it itself.

intentions.title: Layer a second, orthogonal edge-type onto the dependency graph — WHY a file exists (its intention/objective), not just what it imports — so scope/impact analysis can be intention-driven, not just import-driven
intentions.evidence: tooling/intentions/intentions.mjs tags files by objective; tooling/intentions/review.mjs partitions files into subsystem review batches (this very harness); push.mjs emits an `intentions` typed-reference field alongside `dependencies` on each paper; tooling/scope/scope.mjs consumes the intention graph to produce task-scoped context packs.

intentions.title: Never let a missing or stale derived report silently present as a perfect score — absent evidence must be visibly excluded or flagged, not treated as 100/clean
intentions.evidence: quality.mjs comments call out a fixed bug: 'this path was silently empty, hiding 5 confirmed layering violations behind a perfect Architecture score'; covReport/cite default to null/clean-with-caveat rather than fabricated pass; risk.mjs's coverage cache signature (git blob hash + dirty state) forces re-run when source actually changes rather than trusting a stale cache.
